_README: Producer manifest for the closed audit action_type vocabulary (audit Wave 0, guard 2).
THE INERT-CONTROL CLASS THIS CLOSES. ACCEPTED_ACTION_TYPES in
operator/adapter/audit_log.py is a closed enum. Its TS mirror (AUDIT_ACTION_TYPES in
src/lib/portal/operator/audit.ts) is parity-tested, and the dashboard / compliance
evidence packet CONSUME these values (audit viewer filters, compliance.ts roll-ups,
evidence/packet.py _count(...) buckets). But nothing asserted that each consumed
value has a RUNTIME PRODUCER. An action_type can sit in the enum, be mirrored to TS,
be counted by the compliance packet, and be emitted by NOBODY — a dashboard column or
compliance metric that is structurally always-zero. That is the inert-control class:
a consumer with no producer reads as 'feature present, value 0' indistinguishable from
'genuinely zero events'.
WHAT THIS MANIFEST DECLARES. For every action_type in the enum, where its producer
lives. THREE sides:
'ss-console' = a non-test source file in THIS repo emits it (the test asserts the
named producerFile exists and contains the token in code).
'overlay'    = it is emitted by the venturecrane/hermes-smd-overlay runtime that ships
on customer Machines (a separate, pinned repo not checked out in this
CI; we record overlayProducer + reason — the same cross-repo
human-decision shape operator/contracts/overlay-pairs.json uses).
'deferred'   = in the closed vocabulary and CONSUMED (viewer filter / compliance),
but NO producer writes the literal row yet — persistence is gated on a
tracked issue. This is the live inert-control instance the guard found;
it carries producerIntent + reason naming the gap and the unblocking
work, so the always-zero metric is documented loudly, not hidden.
ENFORCEMENT (tests/operator-audit-producers.test.ts):
1. COVERAGE: manifest keys == ACCEPTED_ACTION_TYPES exactly. A new action_type with
no manifest entry fails CI, forcing a conscious producer classification — the gate
that would have caught a consumed-but-never-produced type.
2. ss-console PRODUCERS ARE REAL: each 'ss-console' entry's producerFile exists and
contains the token in code. Deleting the only producer of a still-consumed type
fails CI here.
3. overlay ENTRIES DOCUMENT THE BOUNDARY: each carries overlayProducer + reason, so
the cross-repo producer is named rather than silently assumed.
This is NOT the TS<->Python parity test (that lives in tests/portal-operator-audit.test.ts
and stays). This is the orthogonal producer-existence proof.

DRAFT_CREATED.reason: drafts are authored by the agent at runtime on the Machine; ss-console only reads them back via the drafts surface.

DRAFT_APPROVED.reason: approval is recorded on the Machine when the reviewer approves; the ss-console send-approved.ts surface is a consumer/initiator, not the audit producer.

DRAFT_REJECTED.note: the refusal handler writes DRAFT_REJECTED when a draft is refused by the substrate.

DRAFT_EXPIRED.reason: draft expiry is a Machine-local TTL sweep; no ss-console code path expires a draft.

MEMORY_RULE_ADDED.reason: The portal teach-a-rule producer (teach-marcus) was removed per ADR 0052 (no portal work-actions; the operator learns via its own runtime loop / the conversational channel). Memory rules are now added on the per-customer Machine, like MEMORY_RULE_EDITED.

MEMORY_RULE_EDITED.reason: rule edits land in the per-customer memory store on the Machine; ss-console has no edit producer today.

MEMORY_RULE_DELETED.reason: rule deletes land in the per-customer memory store on the Machine; ss-console has no delete producer today.

TRUST_PROMOTED.reason: trust-ceiling promotions are decided and recorded by the runtime trust plugin.

TRUST_DEMOTED.reason: trust-ceiling demotions are decided and recorded by the runtime trust plugin.

SKILL_ENABLED.reason: skill enable/disable is a Machine-local skill-catalog mutation.

SKILL_DISABLED.reason: skill enable/disable is a Machine-local skill-catalog mutation.

ROUTINE_ENABLED.reason: A routine is turned on by an authored customer.yaml cron entry, materialized at boot by bootstrap/cron_materialize.py. That runs in `hermes-smd bootstrap`, which is NOT the gateway, and the broker gates the generic audit_append on the gateway PID (the GATEWAY class on its row in operator/workspace_broker/verbs.py) -- so bootstrap spools the change to $HERMES_HOME/.smd/routine_changes.jsonl (shared/routine_change_spool.py) and the audit plugin drains it into rows at registration, inside the one process authorized to write the ledger. Emitted on the DELTA only: the materializer recreates every managed job on every boot, so a row per created job would claim a change nobody made at every restart. Actor is `customer.yaml` with actor_role=operator -- the seat sees only the materialized config and must not invent a named person it cannot verify.

ROUTINE_DISABLED.reason: The disable half of the same delta, and the half #2498 was filed for: ashton-price has shipped with `cron: []` since #2332 and the ledger never said so, leaving a deliberately quiet seat indistinguishable from a broken one. Also fires when the ss#2276 cron-containment sentinel converges a seat to zero managed jobs -- that IS a disable, and hiding it would recreate the same confusion.

CONNECTOR_BOUND.reason: connector binding happens during Machine provisioning/runtime; the connections.ts surface is a consumer.

CONNECTOR_UNBOUND.reason: connector unbinding happens on the Machine.

CONNECTOR_AUTH_EXPIRED.reason: auth-expiry is detected by the Machine's connector health probe.

CONNECTOR_AUTH_RESTORED.reason: auth-restore is recorded by the Machine when a token refresh succeeds.

CONNECTOR_TOKEN_REFRESHED.reason: token refresh is a Machine-local connector operation.

CONNECTOR_HEALTH_PROBE_FAILED.reason: health-probe failures are detected on the Machine.

SCOPE_CHANGED.reason: scope changes apply on the Machine via the config sync sidecar.

INVARIANT_VIOLATION.note: WARN/SOFT_STOP transition emits INVARIANT_VIOLATION; invariant_6 also routes here at runtime.

INBOUND_RECEIVED.reason: one row per untrusted inbound item is written by the runtime webhook router as it lands.

RBAC_EVENT.reason: the corrections plugin writes RBAC_EVENT refusal rows (metadata subAction=correction_capture_refused) when a rostered NON-admin's message would have been captured as a standing correction — capture is server-gated on sender_is_admin from the session-keyed verified origin (ss#2429). The ss-console portal writer intent (rbac-audit.ts, user-management actions) remains gated on #821/#891 and unwired; producerIntent is kept so that half is not forgotten.

COMPLIANCE_PACKET_EXPORTED.note: every successful compliance-evidence packet build emits COMPLIANCE_PACKET_EXPORTED.

VOICE_GATE_PASSED.reason: the voice gate runs in the runtime voice plugin on draft emission.

VOICE_GATE_NEAR_PASS.reason: the voice gate runs in the runtime voice plugin on draft emission.

VOICE_GATE_FAILED.reason: the voice gate runs in the runtime voice plugin on draft emission.

FABRICATION_FILTER_TRIGGERED.reason: the fabrication filter runs on the Machine at skill-output time.

IDENTIFIER_UNVERIFIED.reason: the identifier gate runs on the Machine; report-only, non-blocking.

ESCALATION_FIRED.note: the refusal handler fires the Captain escalation cascade.

ESCALATION_ACKNOWLEDGED.overlayProducer: runtime escalation ack path / admin acknowledgement
ESCALATION_ACKNOWLEDGED.reason: escalation acknowledgement is recorded when the alert is acked; no ss-console producer today.

HONCHO_CONCLUSION_DISMISSED.reason: emitted on Captain dismissal in the admin portal via the memory-mirror plugin; the paired physical Honcho DELETE is Machine-side.

AGENT_SKILL_CREATED.reason: agent-authored skills are created at runtime; the audit plugin records them on the Machine.

AGENT_SKILL_REMOVED.reason: agent-skill removal is recorded on the Machine.

CUSTOMER_YAML_SYNCED.reason: the per-Machine config sync sidecar emits this when R2-source customer.yaml changes apply.

CUSTOMER_YAML_STRUCTURAL_CHANGE_DEFERRED.reason: the sidecar logs structural changes as deferred for Captain re-provision.

SUBAGENT_STOPPED.reason: one row per child subagent completion, emitted by the runtime audit plugin.

SUBAGENT_INCOMPLETE.reason: emitted by the parent skill on the Machine before refusing to assemble an incomplete draft.

SUPPRESSED_WAKE.note: Broker-stamped via the uid-gated suppressed_wake_append verb (#1748): skills' pre_run.py (shared empty-seat gate at operator/templates/pre_run_gate.py, plus deadline-miss-escalator's bespoke gate) send the row over the broker socket before printing {wakeAgent:false}. The adapter SuppressedWakeWriter (operator/adapter/audit_log.py) remains the dev/test writer.

EMITTED_WAKE.note: The wake half of the cron gate (#2253). Broker-stamped via the uid-gated emitted_wake_append verb; the producers are the pre_run.py scripts, each attempting the row on the real-decision wake path BEFORE printing {wakeAgent:true}. Written best-effort: unlike SUPPRESSED_WAKE, a write failure must NOT change the decision, so a wake is never gated on its own audit row. The adapter SuppressedWakeWriter.write_emitted_wake (operator/adapter/audit_log.py) remains the dev/test writer. 2026-08-20 (#2498) CORRECTION + WIDENING. The prior note named four producers — deadline-miss-escalator, client-verification-tracker, paid-media-anomaly-watcher, retainer-hours-reconciler — and two of those were wrong: paid-media-anomaly-watcher and retainer-hours-reconciler have no pre_run.py at all, while lien-ledger-tracker and medical-records-chaser (both of which graduated to bespoke gates after the note was written) do produce. Probed, not assumed: `grep -l emitted_wake_append operator/skills/*/pre_run.py` returns exactly client-verification-tracker, deadline-miss-escalator, lien-ledger-tracker, medical-records-chaser. #2498 also carries the wake half to the SHARED gate template (operator/templates/pre_run_gate.py -> write_emitted_wake_heartbeat), which stamps into the eight skills pinned in operator/tests/test_pre_run_gate.py GATED_SKILLS — those eight wrote a row on every quiet tick and nothing on the ticks they fired, so the one tick that mattered was the one tick with no row. Producer count is therefore 12, not 4.

REPLY_SENT.reason: emitted on the customer Machine when the reply channel sends the Operator's governed draft back to a rostered, recipient-locked inbound sender.

REPLY_HELD.reason: emitted on the customer Machine when an autonomous reply is held to draft (off-roster sender, recipient mismatch, content floor, rate-limit, no inbox, empty body, or — since ss#2167 — matter_mismatch, the reply citing a matter its recipient is provably not a party to).

MATTER_UNRESOLVED.reason: emitted on the customer Machine when the outbound matter-identity gate runs on a reply and can neither confirm nor deny that the recipient is a party to the cited matter, because the matter's party list was never read that turn. Recorded rather than held: get_matter fires on 8 of 86 reply turns (vfy_01KZRRWG2WZKTRNZQRDEX494GZ), so holding on unresolved would withhold correct client replies at an unmeasured rate; these rows are that measurement.

REPLY_FAILED.reason: emitted on the customer Machine when the AgentMail reply send is attempted but errors (HTTP / unreachable / timeout).

TOOL_CALL_COMPLETED.reason: one row per tool invocation on the customer Machine; the highest-volume type on both seats (~69% of pilot rows, live-probed 2026-08-02).

LLM_TURN_COMPLETED.reason: one row per completed agent turn; does not fire on interrupted turns (documented in the overlay's docs/hook-surface.md).

WEBHOOK_ROUTED.reason: one row per inbound webhook successfully routed to a skill; payload source + event_type in metadata.

WEBHOOK_SUPPRESSED.reason: one row per suppressed inbound; the suppression stands whether or not the audit write succeeds (gate comment webhook_gate.py:440-443).

BROKER_DECISION_ALLOWED.reason: decision row written before mediated-connector grant redemption.

BROKER_EXECUTED.reason: execution row paired with broker-signed receipt evidence.

CONFIG_WRITE.reason: one row per live customer.yaml apply; digests carry old/new config provenance, never content.

CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED.note: written by the broker's own _dispatch_transmit (overlay#256 moved it off the plugin; claims review 2026-09-04 B3 corrected this entry, which still named the overlay). The overlay contributes stamps on audit_extra; the row itself is the broker's.

CONFIRM_SEND_FAILED.note: the refusal / transport-error sibling of CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED, written by the same _dispatch_transmit; same producer, same correction.

SPEC_GATE_TRIGGERED.reason: emitted when output fails the client-authored format spec.

VOICE_GATE_TRIGGERED.reason: report-only voice-gate signal; distinct from VOICE_GATE_PASSED/NEAR_PASS/FAILED which have no emitter.

CORRECTION_PROPOSED.reason: the workspace broker appends the client-correction capture row directly to the Machine ledger (ss#2091); declared in both vocabularies 2026-08-02 (#2122) so ledger contents are never outside the closed set.

RULE_PROPOSED.reason: ss#2529. The workspace broker appends one row per rule the Operator states back for confirmation. Nothing is installed by it: the row records that a sentence was put in front of a person with a tag, carrying the proposal id and the text digest and never the text. The confirming turn writes ESTABLISHMENT_SUBMITTED under the same digest, so the two rows together prove the committed rule is the proposed one without either of them holding a copy of it.

ESTABLISHMENT_SUBMITTED.reason: ss#2161 (ADR 0085). The broker appends this when an establishment run is materialized into the root intake spool, on all three scopes (firm, person, firm_adjust). Declared in this repo 2026-08-21 (ss#2529): it had been landing in client ledgers since establishment shipped while AUDIT_ACTION_TYPES had never heard of it, so the portal rendered it as nothing.

ESTABLISHMENT_RESULT.reason: ss#2161 (ADR 0085). The broker appends the bounded verdict row on the one-shot result read, before deleting the result file, so the retained trace outlives the payload. Declared in this repo 2026-08-21 (ss#2529), same history as ESTABLISHMENT_SUBMITTED.

RULE_REQUEST_NOTIFIED.reason: ss#2546. The establishment plugin emits this when a non-admin's firm-level rule has actually been EMAILED to the administrators the firm names on scope.rule_requests_to, carrying who was notified and never the rule's text. Its own row rather than a field on the send's CONFIRM_SEND_DISPATCHED row, because the two answer different questions: the send row says a message left, this says a specific request reached the people authorized to answer it, which is what anyone auditing this loop is looking for. WAS side: deferred for exactly one release (ss#2546 PR 1 declared the type before its producer existed, so the client feed would render the first row ever written rather than the ss#2316 silence); it becomes overlay-produced at the OVERLAY_REF bump to 119f6bf2 (overlay#311), which returns the deferred count to zero.

MEDCHRON_JOB_SUBMITTED.reason: ss#2614 routine 11. The workspace broker appends one row when a chronology-package job is submitted (by the Operator through medchron_job_submit, or by root on the box). Carries the job id, the matter number, the unit count and the allowance remainder; never the envelope.

MEDCHRON_JOB_RUNNING.reason: ss#2614. The runner daemon reports through the broker (medchron_job_record, uid 0 only) and the broker writes the row: the run started, or resumed after a seat-pause hold.

MEDCHRON_JOB_HELD.reason: ss#2614. The run stopped and surfaced why: a seat at HARD_STOP, an unexplained file, an unmatched folder, or a refusal (the cents cap, the monthly allowance). The reason is prose in metadata.

MEDCHRON_JOB_DELIVERED.reason: ss#2614. The package is on the matter: documents read, pages, cents, the folder id, and the file names with sha256 and byte counts the runner read back.

MEDCHRON_JOB_FAILED.reason: ss#2614. The runner exited without a verdict or a stage failed; the reason is the runner's own sentence.

ACT_PROPOSED.reason: ss#2536. The workspace broker appends one row per ACT the Operator states back for confirmation. Nothing happens by it: the row records that one tool call was put in front of a Named Administrator with a tag, carrying the proposal id, the tool name, and the payload digest, and never the payload. The confirming turn writes ACT_COMMITTED under the same digest, so the two rows together prove the act performed is the act proposed without either of them holding a second copy of the firm's values.

ACT_COMMITTED.reason: ss#2536. Appended after the confirmed tool call succeeded, naming who confirmed it and the message id their confirmation arrived in, so an admin approval is joinable to the inbound row that carried it (the ss#2497 joins) rather than merely asserted. A tool call that failed writes no row: the proposal stays open for its TTL, so a transport failure does not spend a person's yes.

RULE_DECLINED.reason: ss#2546. The broker appends one row when an administrator refuses a rule somebody else asked for. Before this verb a "no" did nothing at all: the rule sat open until it expired and the only record of the decision was whatever the model happened to say in a reply. The row carries the proposal id, who stated the rule, who declined it, and the text digest - never the sentence - so it joins to RULE_PROPOSED on the digest and the ledger shows WHICH rule was refused without holding a second copy of the firm's words. Written under a conditional UPDATE, so a second decline changes nothing and writes nothing.

RULE_LAPSED.reason: ss#2546. The broker appends this when the person who asked for a rule has been TOLD it lapsed unanswered, not when the sweep marks it. That ordering is the point: the mark is bookkeeping, the row is the moment the firm learned something. A lapse has no other row anywhere - nothing was committed and nobody decided - so this is the only record that a request died, which is why the sweep now marks an expired row instead of deleting it. Reporting a DECLINE writes nothing here: RULE_DECLINED already recorded that decision.

OPS_REQUEST_RECORDED.reason: ss#2546 (the operations half). The broker appends one row when somebody at the firm asks for a change only SMD makes - a routine, a schedule, a channel, a memory setting, an autonomy level, an on/off (ADR 0085 as amended 2026-08-22). Nothing is changed by it: the row records that a request was given an [ops XXXX] tag so SMD's answer can find its way back to the person who asked, and it carries the proposal id, who asked, and the text digest - never the sentence. The answering row joins to it on that digest.

OPS_REQUEST_RESOLVED.reason: ss#2546 (the operations half). Appended when SMD answers a request through ops_resolve, naming the outcome (done / declined / withdrawn) and who at SMD answered, under a conditional UPDATE so a second answer changes nothing and writes nothing. The reason SMD wrote is NOT retained here - only has_reason, a countable fact - because it is a person's prose about a business decision and retained rows carry ids, names, and counts (ADR 0083).

OPS_REQUEST_LAPSED.reason: ss#2546 (the operations half). Appended when the person who asked has been TOLD their request to SMD lapsed unanswered, not when the sweep marks it - the mark is bookkeeping, the row is the moment the firm learned something. Its own type rather than RULE_LAPSED because nobody at the firm failed to answer it: SMD did, and a ledger filing the two under one name would misattribute the silence. A resolved request writes nothing here; OPS_REQUEST_RESOLVED already recorded that answer.
